words.d: to make something by combining parts
the work of making something from parts
a tool for hitting nails
small sticks that make fire when struck
to stir things together so they become one
a planned piece of work that takes time
a thick strong cord made of twisted strands
a small stretchy loop that holds things together
a thing you hold to help you fix or make things
a solid piece of something with flat sides
a long flat piece of sawn timber
a sheet put over a thing to shelter it
the side that faces forward
to make better
a case holding a set of things you need

videos.desc: A group of friends in a field measures and marks planks, drills them together, raises wall frames, and step by step builds a complete wooden shed, celebrating together in front of the finished build.
videos.said: We build a wooden shed. It is a big project.

videos.desc: A couple at a community garden builds a raised wooden planter: they hold the frame square, screw the boards together with a cordless drill, check the top with a spirit level, fill it with soil from a wheelbarrow and plant two seedlings, finishing with a high-five.
videos.said: Hold it square, go! Dead level!

videos.desc: First-person view into a blue bucket as a hand folds and stirs thick pale joint compound with a putty knife. The paste is scooped, turned and smoothed over and over until it looks creamy, in a slow oddly satisfying rhythm.

In a garage workshop a man sets a nail on the roof of a small wooden birdhouse and drives it in with careful hammer taps while a friend watches; he runs his hand over the flush nail head and the two fist-bump over the finished build.

In a cozy wooden cabin at night, a woman slides open a box of matches, takes one out and strikes it, and it flares up on the first try while her friend watches. She uses the burning match to light an oil lamp on the table, then drops the spent match into a clay pot.
videos.said: (upbeat music) - One good strike. (gasps) - First try. (upbeat music)

videos.desc: A cartoon farmer carries a coil of rope, knots it around the wheel of a cart stuck in mud, and pulls hard together with a second farmer until the cart jerks free and both tumble laughing onto the grass, rope in hand.
videos.said: Tight. Very tight. Ready? Heave! It's coming! It's coming! Woo-hoo!

videos.desc: At a market herb stall, a young woman stretches an orange rubber band wide between her thumbs while a man watches amazed, then she snaps it around a bundle of fresh cilantro to hold the stems together and lifts the tied bunch.

Two men fix a bicycle mounted upside down outdoors next to a pegboard hung with tools; one grabs pliers and gets told "nope, wrong one", then browses the wrenches, screwdriver and hammer, picks the right wrench and holds it up grinning before turning the bolt.
videos.said: Nope, wrong one. That one, done.

videos.desc: A close shot of an unfinished wall built from large pale building blocks with thin mortar joints between them, under a window that looks out over a foggy green field. A hand in a grey work glove holds a cut-off clear plastic bottle flat against the blocks, directly under the tip of a drill. The drill bores into the block and the grey dust falls straight down into the bottle instead of onto the floor. When the drilling stops, the hand lifts the bottle away to show a neat round hole in the block and a heap of grey dust collected inside the bottle.

A close overhead shot outdoors. A pale wooden board with a round hole cut through the middle is laid flat across the top of a big carved wooden bowl, with a crate of whole walnuts behind it. A hand picks a walnut out of the crate and sets it in the hole in the board so it sits held in place. A hammer swings down and cracks the walnut; the pieces of shell and the kernel drop straight through the hole into the bowl underneath. The hand fetches another walnut and does it again, and the bowl below slowly fills up with broken shells and pale nut kernels.

Two old sports cars stand nose to nose on a concrete driveway in front of a tall green hedge. The camera holds on the front of an orange car on the left, with its round chrome headlight and chrome mirror, and the front of a yellow car on the right, with its indicator and chrome bumper. The camera moves slowly so the two fronts almost touch in the middle of the frame. At the end a man in dark blue overalls and a cap leans over the front of the yellow car and works on it.

A dark flat with no power. A woman in a yellow hard hat with a headlamp stands at a wall panel, holding a pair of pliers and a bundle of coloured wires. Close-ups show gloved hands stripping a red wire and pushing it into a circuit breaker set into a broken-open wall box. A family stands in the dark hallway behind her lighting the corridor with phone torches. She works at the fuse panel, then turns to the camera smiling as the flat lights come back on.

A man in a work shirt builds a wooden fence across a sunny back garden. He holds a squared timber post upright, then screws a horizontal rail into it with a cordless drill. He knocks a post into place with a yellow rubber mallet along a run of fence that already carries rows of vertical palings, checks the top rail with a spirit level, and works along a string line pegged into the fresh soil. At the end the finished fence runs the full length of the lawn and he leans over the top of it and smiles.

On a trestle table in a sunny garden a man taps a hammer against a small wooden birdhouse, holding a finger over the round entrance hole. He steps back and turns the finished birdhouse, with its pitched roof, little porch and railings, to the camera. Cut to a lawn where about eight people crouch around a huge folded grey tarpaulin and spread it out flat. Then the same group heave a tall triangular timber wall frame upright, and finally they stand back on the grass looking up at the finished wooden house frame standing on its slab.

In a bright flat a young woman points up at a ceiling fitting whose bare bulb is dead. She and a young man carry in an aluminium stepladder and open it under the fitting; she climbs the steps while he steadies the frame, screws a new bulb into the socket and it lights up warm and bright. They look up at the working light, then fold the ladder away.

An empty room being redecorated: the furniture is hidden under grey plastic sheeting and the floor is spread with white dust sheets. A young man in paint-spattered dungarees, headphones round his neck, rolls terracotta paint over a grey wall with a roller on a pole. He works across and up until the whole wall is orange, then reaches up and starts peeling the masking tape off the top edge.

Two people in paint-spattered dungarees work on a wrecked room whose walls are bare plaster with old paint peeling off in sheets. One hammers at a battered built-in shelf unit, the woman rolls fresh paint onto a wall while the man smooths the plaster beside her with a trowel, the camera pans across the wet cream paint, and then the same room appears finished: smooth painted walls, new wooden shelves, a plant and a clean tiled floor, with the two of them standing in it looking pleased.

A woman in a denim shirt and a patterned headband stands in an open garage with a wooden kitchen chair in front of her; she presses on the seat and it wobbles. She turns to a red hard case on the bench and opens it: inside, held in moulded slots, are rows of screwdrivers, spanners, pliers and sockets. She lifts one screwdriver out of the case, tightens the loose joint under the chair, stands the chair back up and sits down on it to show it holds.

On a misty country road in the rain, dogs in hard hats and high-visibility vests work on an old cream bus with its bonnet open. One dog in a yellow hat lies on a mechanic's creeper and reaches a spanner towards an engine block on a tarp. One in a white hat stands on a metal lifting rig whose chain holds up the engine, and another in a yellow hat shines a small lamp. More dogs sit on the roof and in the driver's seat. Tools lie on the tarp, and a young woman with an umbrella watches.

A new steel footbridge over a deep river gorge at sunrise. The two halves of the bridge meet in the middle, and a young woman in a white hard hat, orange high-visibility jacket and safety harness kneels on the steel grating, tightening the bolts on the plate that joins them with a big wrench. Across the gap a worker welds the seam in a shower of sparks. She then sits up and raises her fist with a shout, and workers in hard hats cheer on both sides. Two tall cranes stand on the cliffs and a safety net hangs below.

On a sunny street of terraced houses, a young woman in paint-splattered white overalls stands on scaffolding with a roller, covering her mouth in shock. The view pulls back to show that the whole house has been painted bright pink, even its chimney, while the grey house next door is untouched. Another painter in overalls stands by the gate below, a woman looks out of the door, and on the pavement a young man in a straw hat and neck pillow, with two suitcases, stares up at the pink house.

A roof being built high above an old town at sunset. A bearded carpenter in a white helmet, white shirt, black waistcoat and safety harness stands on a huge square beam of pale solid oak that hangs from a crane hook, and swings an axe into it so wood chips fly. The cut end shows its tree rings clearly. The beam then comes to rest on a wooden post. Below him young apprentices in black hold wooden mallets on the scaffolding next to rows of new rafters, and a church spire rises behind.
